review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

2:1.sourceText: Σὺ οὖν, τέκνον μου, ἐνδυναμοῦ ἐν τῇ χάριτι τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,
2:1.targetText: You, therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that [is] in Christ Jesus,

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

2:2.sourceText: καὶ ἃ ἤκουσας παρ’ ἐμοῦ διὰ πολλῶν μαρτύρων, ταῦτα παράθου πιστοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οἵτινες ἱκανοὶ ἔσονται καὶ ἑτέρους διδάξαι.
2:2.targetText: and the things that you heard from me through many witnesses, be committing these things to steadfast men, who will also be sufficient to teach others;

2:3.sourceText: συνκακοπάθησον ὡς καλὸς στρατιώτης Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
2:3.targetText: you, therefore, suffer evil as a good soldier of Jesus Christ;

groups.note: The actual N1904 second-person imperative συγκακοπάθησον is share in hardship, supplying English you and containing the together/with prefix; LSV simply says suffer evil and follows TR κακοπάθησον. The common hardship predicate is retained with the source’s unexpressed shared-participation nuance explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective addition: LSV therefore follows TR οὖν, absent before the single shared-suffering imperative in N1904. TR also prints an explicit σὺ, but the actual N1904 second-person imperative itself supports the English you subject without another Greek pronoun.

review.note: Jesus Christ reverses the N1904 Christ Jesus title/name order; actual name identities are preserved.

2:4.sourceText: οὐδεὶς στρατευόμενος ἐμπλέκεται ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις, ἵνα τῷ στρατολογήσαντι ἀρέσῃ.
2:4.targetText: no one serving as a soldier entangles himself with the affairs of life, that he may please him who enlisted him;

groups.note: The middle verb ἐμπλέκεται expresses becoming involved/entangling oneself; English himself is the rendering of that middle predicate, not a separate Greek reflexive pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the recruited soldier object explicit as him after enlisted; no independent Greek object pronoun is written with that recruiting participle.

2:5.sourceText: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἀθλῇ τις, οὐ στεφανοῦται ἐὰν μὴ νομίμως ἀθλήσῃ.
2:5.targetText: and if anyone also may strive, he is not crowned, except he may strive lawfully;

groups.note: The conditional plus negative ἐὰν μή means unless; LSV uses except to express the same necessary condition of lawful competition.

2:6.sourceText: τὸν κοπιῶντα γεωργὸν δεῖ πρῶτον τῶν καρπῶν μεταλαμβάνειν.
2:6.targetText: it is first necessary [for] the laboring farmer to partake of the fruits;

groups.note: The actual accusative article/farmer phrase is the subject of the partaking infinitive under δεῖ, it is necessary. English expresses that case-marked subject as for the farmer; the for relation belongs to the whole noun phrase, not a separately printed Greek preposition. The intervening laboring participle retains its own lexical anchor.

2:7.sourceText: νόει ὃ λέγω· δώσει γάρ σοι ὁ Κύριος σύνεσιν ἐν πᾶσιν.
2:7.targetText: be considering what things I say, for the LORD gives to you understanding in all things.

groups.note: Pinned N1904 δώσει is future will give, whereas LSV prints present gives; TR has the optative δῴη. The same giving action remains linked with these form differences explicit.

2:12.sourceText: εἰ ὑπομένομεν, καὶ συνβασιλεύσομεν· εἰ ἀρνησόμεθα, κἀκεῖνος ἀρνήσεται ἡμᾶς·
2:12.targetText: if we endure together—we will also reign together; if we deny [Him], He will also deny us;

groups.note: N1904 ἀρνησόμεθα is future we will deny, while LSV prints we deny as in TR present ἀρνούμεθα. The denial predicate remains shared with the tense difference explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds together to the first endure predicate. N1904 ὑπομένομεν, like TR, has no together prefix or separate together word; the later reigning compound genuinely supplies its own together.
Bracketed English makes the denied object explicit; no independent Him object pronoun is written at we-deny in N1904.

2:13.sourceText: εἰ ἀπιστοῦμεν, ἐκεῖνος πιστὸς μένει, ἀρνήσασθαι γὰρ ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται.
2:13.targetText: if we are not steadfast, He remains steadfast; He is not able to deny Himself.

unmappedSource.reason: The explanatory γάρ before the inability-to-deny statement is not separately expressed in LSV, which starts a new sentence He is not able.

2:18.sourceText: οἵτινες περὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἠστόχησαν, λέγοντες ἀνάστασιν ἤδη γεγονέναι, καὶ ἀνατρέπουσιν τήν τινων πίστιν.
2:18.targetText: who swerved concerning the truth, saying the resurrection to have already been, and overthrows the faith of some;

groups.note: The actual Greek overturning verb ἀνατρέπουσιν is third-person plural, they overthrow, whereas displayed LSV has singular overthrows. The same action is linked with this agreement wording difference explicit.

2:20.sourceText: ἐν μεγάλῃ δὲ οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔστιν μόνον σκεύη χρυσᾶ καὶ ἀργυρᾶ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ξύλινα καὶ ὀστράκινα, καὶ ἃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν ἃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν·
2:20.targetText: And in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth, and some to honor, and some to dishonor:

review.note: The material adjectives golden/silver/wooden/earthen are rendered as of gold/of silver/of wood/of earth. Their actual adjective heads remain distinct; no extra Greek material nouns or of prepositions are invented. The relative/μέν distribution is rendered some ... and some.

2:21.sourceText: ἐὰν οὖν τις ἐκκαθάρῃ ἑαυτὸν ἀπὸ τούτων, ἔσται σκεῦος εἰς τιμήν, ἡγιασμένον, εὔχρηστον τῷ δεσπότῃ, εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἡτοιμασμένον.
2:21.targetText: if, then, anyone may cleanse himself from these, he will be a vessel to honor, sanctified and profitable to the master—having been prepared to every good work;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness conjunction addition: LSV and profitable follows TR καί before profitable; N1904 proceeds directly from sanctified to profitable.

2:22.targetText: and flee the youthful lusts, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace, with those calling on the LORD out of a pure heart;

2:23.targetText: and be avoiding the foolish and uninstructed questions, having known that they beget strife,

2:24.sourceText: δοῦλον δὲ Κυρίου οὐ δεῖ μάχεσθαι ἀλλὰ ἤπιον εἶναι πρὸς πάντας, διδακτικόν, ἀνεξίκακον,
2:24.targetText: and a servant of the LORD must not quarrel, but to be gentle to all, apt to teach, patient under evil,

2:25.sourceText: ἐν πραΰτητι παιδεύοντα τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους, μή ποτε δώῃ αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς μετάνοιαν εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας,

groups.note: The μήποτε expression introduces the tentative hope whether/perhaps God may grant conversion; LSV renders if perhaps. Its negative-form particle belongs to that idiomatic tentative construction, not an unexpressed assertion that God will not grant it.
The change-of-mind/repentance noun μετάνοια is rendered conversion by LSV here; the actual repentance head is retained without inventing a separate turning verb.
